messages:
Samir Patel: 16:10 UTC — opening thread. We're seeing a sustained spike in 5xx and client timeouts to hosted inference API in us-west-2. Dashboard: https://redwood.ops/d/alerts/5067
OpsBot: [ALERT] hosted-gateway 5xx rate increased 4.2x in last 7m (503/504). Avg p95 latency > 2s.
Ellie Chen: quick heads-up — auth-proxy is returning 502 errors to the gateway. Correlates with auth-cache evictions. I see many token refresh calls around the same time.
Marco Ruiz: Repro logs show repeated /token/refresh calls for same client ids — looks like a token refresh storm after our recent JWT TTL change.
Julie Park: Can we throttle token refreshes at the proxy level? If we don't stop the refresh loop it keeps spiking backend.
Miranda Lee: I'm pausing the heavy customer (cust-42) traffic at the routing layer — setting route to maintenance for 5m.
Marco Ruiz: Starting canary rollback of jwt_ttl config (old=60s, new=10s). Rolling back on 10% cluster now. Command:
```
kubectl -n hosted apply -f auth-proxy-config-canary.yaml
# jwt_ttl: 60s
```
Ellie Chen: Noted. Also seeing KMS returning 429s concurrently. Could be backend KMS throttle causing token refresh failures.
Samir Patel: Action: Marco roll back jwt_ttl fully if canary looks good. Julie enable per-client refresh backoff. Miranda keep cust-42 paused until we confirm stability.
Marco Ruiz: Canary looks good after 4m — 5xx rate dropped ~55% on canary nodes. Rolling full rollback now. :thumbsup: 
OpsBot: [EVENT] rollback completed at 16:22 UTC — config-version v1.8.3 (previous v1.9.0)
Ellie Chen: After rollback, gateway 5xxs are trending down but p95 latencies still elevated. KMS 429s persist for another ~10m.
Julie Park: I've deployed a temporary circuit-breaker rule to limit token refresh attempts per client: backoff=exponential, max_retries=3.
Miranda Lee: Re-enabled cust-42 routing to canary traffic at 16:32 UTC — no errors observed so far.
Samir Patel: Good containment. For postmortem: we need root cause (why jwt_ttl change caused storm), improve canary gating, and KMS throttling mitigation.
Ellie Chen: Quick notes on repro steps:
- config change: jwt_ttl -> 10s
- within minutes clients scheduled token renewal at same time -> many simultaneous /token/refresh
- auth-proxy does not debounce identical refreshes -> each request calls KMS
- KMS throttle -> token refresh failures -> gateway retries -> more load
Logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T16:11:05Z auth-proxy [warn] token refresh failed status=429 k=projects/xyz
2026-03-17T16:11:05Z gateway [error] upstream 502 for req_id=abc123
```
Marco Ruiz: Immediate mitigations applied: rollback jwt_ttl, per-client refresh backoff, route pause for largest customers, temporary rate-limits. All applied by 16:25 UTC.
Julie Park: Postmortem action items (owners + ETA):
- A1: Revisit jwt_ttl rollout process + stricter canary gating (owner: Marco Ruiz) — due in 48h
- A2: Implement debounce on identical /token/refresh per-client for 60s (owner: Ellie Chen) — due in 7 days
- A3: Cloud provider KMS request pattern review and quota increase options (owner: Julie Park) — due in 72h
- A4: Add synthetic load test for token refresh path to CI (owner: Miranda Lee) — due in 10 days
- A5: Customer communication draft + RCA (owner: Samir Patel) — due in 48h
Samir Patel: Can each owner confirm and add a jira ticket by EOW. I'll start postmortem doc and invite ops/research to review.
Miranda Lee: Confirmed. Jira for A1: INF-2456
Marco Ruiz: Confirmed. Jira for A2: INF-2457
Ellie Chen: Added INF-2458 for debounce + tests.
Julie Park: INF-2459 for KMS review.
OpsBot: [NOTE] Incident severity: P1 -> downgraded to P2 at 16:40 UTC; channel on-call cleared.
Samir Patel: Final check-in: if numbers remain stable for 30m we'll close war room and transition to postmortem doc. Thanks all for quick responses. :rocket:
Ellie Chen: Agreed — monitoring for 30m, will update.
Marco Ruiz: Leaving a couple of follow-up checks overnight for rollout safety.
Miranda Lee: I'll schedule customer follow-ups tomorrow morning PT.
Samir Patel: Closing the thread for live ops. Postmortem draft link: https://redwood.docs/postmortems/inf-2026-03-17-auth-cache-storm
